report.source_text: Considering physical examination, the patient had complete bilateral horizontal gaze palsy in the horizontal plane while vertical gaze was normal, aside from slightly decreased velocity of saccadic movements. Pupils were midsize and reactive, and nystagmus, diplopia or blurry vision were not found. Mild bilateral peripheral facial nerve palsy was also presented in the physical exam. Hyperreflexia in all four limbs was detectable without clonus, plantar reflexes were down going, and muscle forces were not reduced. There were no apparent signs of spasticity and ataxia. All other physical exam findings were normal.

clinician.current_trajectory_hypothesis: 16-year-old Iranian girl presenting with acute bilateral horizontal gaze palsy (brainstem sign) and progressive ascending paresthesias over months. Neurological exam shows complete bilateral horizontal gaze palsy, mild bilateral facial nerve palsy, and hyperreflexia in all four limbs without motor weakness or spasticity. This clinical picture is consistent with demyelinating disease affecting brainstem and spinal cord. MS diagnosis by McDonald's 2017 criteria requires demonstration of dissemination in space (lesions in ≥2 CNS locations) and time (lesions of different ages or simultaneous asymptomatic enhancing and non-enhancing lesions). MRI findings are critical to establish these criteria.

report.source_text: Magnetic resonance imaging indicated multiple hyperintense subcortical, and periventricular lesions visible on the fluid-attenuated inversion recovery (FLAIR) and T2-weighted images, in addition to bilaterally involving PPRF at the level of the pons, anterior to the cerebral aqueduct (Figs. 1-a, b). Two hyperintense lesions were also presented in the sagittal sections of the spinal MRI, one at the level of C7 and the other adjacent to T4. The lesions visible on the MRI were consistent with demyelination. After gadolinium injection, the PPRF lesions were not enhanced, however, T4 thoracic spine lesion was enhanced.

clinician.current_trajectory_hypothesis: 16-year-old Iranian girl with acute bilateral horizontal gaze palsy (PPRF lesion at pons level) and progressive ascending paresthesias over months (spinal cord lesions at C7 and T4). MRI shows multiple subcortical and periventricular lesions plus brainstem involvement, with disseminated lesions in space (brain, brainstem, spinal cord) and time (non-enhancing PPRF vs. enhancing T4 lesion). This satisfies McDonald's 2017 criteria for dissemination in space and time. CSF analysis with oligoclonal bands would provide additional paraclinical evidence supporting demyelinating disease diagnosis.

clinician.final_diagnosis: Multiple Sclerosis (MS) diagnosed according to 2017 revised McDonald's criteria
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 16-year-old Iranian girl presented with sudden-onset bilateral horizontal gaze palsy developing overnight, superimposed on a 2-month history of progressive ascending paresthesias (feet to trunk) and a prior episode of hand paresthesias 1 year earlier. Neurological examination revealed complete bilateral horizontal gaze palsy with normal vertical gaze, mild bilateral peripheral facial nerve palsy, and hyperreflexia in all four limbs without motor weakness or spasticity. MRI brain and spinal cord demonstrated multiple hyperintense subcortical and periventricular lesions on FLAIR and T2-weighted images, bilateral PPRF involvement at the pons level (anterior to cerebral aqueduct), and spinal cord lesions at C7 and T4 levels. Critically, the PPRF lesions were non-enhancing while the T4 thoracic lesion showed gadolinium enhancement, establishing dissemination in time. The combination of two clinical attacks at different CNS sites (brainstem/brain and spinal cord) confirmed by MRI, along with an enhancing lesion, satisfied the 2017 McDonald's criteria for MS diagnosis. The patient was treated with intravenous methylprednisolone 1000 mg daily for 3 consecutive days, with significant improvement in eye movements by 1 week and complete recovery of ocular movements by 1-month follow-up.
